title: Keep Claude permission blockers dominant across parallel tool completion
description: A normal hcom claude run in finance-sync-mcp issued parallel Read calls. Reading /home/imi/.config/finance-sync/config.json opened Claude's approval UI. hcom emitted blocked:approval, but completion of the sibling repository-local Read transitioned the shared instance row to active:approved Read. The unresolved external-read prompt then remained hidden for 25 minutes while list and compact heartbeat output falsely reported an active worker. The Claude transcript ends with the external Read tool_use and no matching tool_result; the captured terminal log contains the permission menu. Current handle_posttooluse clears any blocked instance without proving that the completed tool owns the pending approval, and the single instance status cannot safely represent interleaved parallel tool lifecycles.
acceptance_criteria: An unresolved Claude PermissionRequest remains visibly blocked/attention-required until that specific approval is resolved or the terminal is demonstrably no longer at approval UI; PostToolUse/PostToolUseFailure/PermissionDenied for a sibling parallel tool cannot clear it; hcom list, compact stream, and waits surface the blocker; regression tests cover two parallel Reads where one completes and the other remains at an external-path permission prompt, including out-of-order hook delivery.
close_reason: Verified fix: Claude approvals are recorded atomically with owner/detail/generation tokens; sibling completion/failure/denial, late PreToolUse, non-approval restore paths, legacy notifications, and PTY edges use write-time guards so replacement approvals remain visible. PTY refusal mirrors actual row state and DB failures are logged. Regression coverage includes parallel Reads, stale snapshots, replacement approvals, missing tool IDs, PTY races, legacy coexistence, and DB error handling. Worker full serial suite 2462/2462 + cli_smoke 60/60; parent approval/restore tests, cargo check, strict clippy, fmt, and diff checks pass.

title: Provide a completion bridge for sandboxed Agy workflows
description:
Historical isolation finding from the 2026-09-07 hcom-f6g.12 run: the then-current user-created hcom run agy workflow explicitly launched Antigravity with --sandbox, while ordinary hcom agy did not. Antigravity provider-native sandbox failed and the safe proceed-in-sandbox policy denied command execution rather than permitting a host bypass, so the worker could not run its prompt-mandated hcom send completion command. The forced --sandbox flag was removed from the user workflow on 2026-09-08; this issue now applies only to the future hcom-owned isolated-workspace rollout and is not a current ordinary run-agy defect.

## Steps to Reproduce
Historical only until the hcom-owned isolation runtime exists: launch an Agy workflow inside the approved isolation boundary, complete useful work while ordinary provider shell execution is unavailable, and verify whether the outer coordinator can still receive an authoritative attempt-bound result without terminal intervention. Do not re-enable the removed provider-native --sandbox flag to reproduce this.
acceptance_criteria: Before isolated Agy workflows are enabled for daily use, their hcom result path remains available inside the approved isolation boundary or is published by the outer coordinator without requiring a provider shell command. A sandbox failure remains fail-closed, never requests or grants host bypass, and returns a typed incomplete-turn or recovery outcome. Deterministic result-bridge tests and an isolated live Antigravity run pass without terminal injection.
notes: Difficulty assessment 2026-09-08: not a standalone current run-agy repair after removal of the forced provider sandbox. It belongs to the future hcom-owned isolation rollout, primarily OpenSpec tasks 5.1-5.2 and 6.2-6.3, and depends on hcom-f6g.3/hcom-f6g.4 infrastructure. Implementation crosses private workflow state, result correlation, PTY/runtime boundary, provider adapter policy, cleanup ordering, and containment/live tests; treat as hard security-sensitive integration work and split along the existing OpenSpec task boundaries.

title: Resume Antigravity delivery after an approval denial
description: During the 2026-09-07 hcom-f6g.12 Agy implementation run, denying Antigravity's sandbox-bypass dialog cleared the provider prompt but left hcom lifecycle state stale. A targeted hcom send was persisted yet did not schedule a new turn, forcing direct PTY prompt injection. This is the Antigravity counterpart to the Claude-specific denial recovery proven under tracker item 36.
acceptance_criteria: After any recognized Antigravity approval denial, hcom detects the settled actionable prompt, transitions the matching generation out of blocked/active state, and schedules exactly one already-queued targeted delivery without direct PTY injection. Newer provider transitions and still-visible approval menus remain protected; deterministic tests and one live run pass.
notes: Difficulty assessment 2026-09-08: likely superseded by hcom-f6g.12 rather than an independent implementation bug. The observed failure used the pre-fix binary, which never classified the approval, so injected denial had no PTY approval state to clear. Current code synchronously clears recognized injected approvals to listening and the focused sandbox-bypass falling-edge plus clear-injection tests pass. Do not implement speculatively; first run one targeted live denial-and-queued-follow-up reproduction. If it still fails, expected patch scope is narrow-to-medium in src/pty/shared.rs/screen.rs plus delivery integration tests.
close_reason: Live verification with the freshly built f6g.12 code proved no independent bug remains. A raw Gemini 3.8 Flash High worker entered blocked/pty:approval for an outside-workspace file request; a targeted follow-up was queued while blocked; denying option 3 published pty:approval_cleared and listening; delivery then transitioned the same generation to active and the worker returned F6G13_RESUMED without direct PTY prompt injection. Focused approval falling-edge and injected-clear tests pass. The earlier failure used the pre-f6g.12 binary, which had never classified the approval.

title: Make result waits terminate on actionable worker blockers
description: A raw Antigravity launch batch reported ready, then the worker entered pty:approval immediately. The coordinator's hcom events --result-from wait remained silent because it watches only terminal results, so it could wait until the full task deadline while no work occurs. A separate blocked wait is race-prone when the transition occurs before its cursor is captured.
acceptance_criteria: One high-level or composable wait can atomically return the correlated workflow result, a typed actionable blocker, launch failure, stopped-without-result state, or deadline. It cannot miss a blocker between readiness and wait registration, and its structured outcome preserves worker generation, workflow thread, attempt cursor, blocker evidence, and recovery guidance.
notes: Live Antigravity Claude Opus attempt on 2026-09-06 did not reach code work. agy sandbox reported a connection issue on 'bd prime', retried 'bd show hcom-f6g.11', then requested permission to bypass the sandbox for that harmless read. hcom remained active/tool:run_command for over 224 seconds instead of surfacing pty:approval; the high-level wrapper stayed silent until the parent inspected the terminal and terminated the worker. No bypass was approved and no files were edited. This reproduces the result-or-blocker observability gap the issue must fix.
close_reason: Implemented one cursor-anchored correlated wait for exact result, typed blocker, launch failure, stopped-without-result, or deadline. Structured outcomes preserve generation/thread/cursor/evidence/recovery. Added race, resolution, generation-reuse, final-poll, payload, and CLI exit-code coverage. Focused tests, workspace check, strict Clippy, and two independent reviews passed; broad suite reached 2306 passed with two unrelated environment-dependent existing failures.

title: Schedule idle Antigravity turns after hcom delivery
description: A targeted hcom send to an idle Antigravity worker inserted the message into the TUI prompt and returned success, but left the worker in listening/tui:prompt-has-text without submitting the prompt. No active transition occurred within a bounded 60-second wait, requiring hcom term inject --enter.
acceptance_criteria: Targeted delivery to a supported idle Antigravity prompt either submits and schedules exactly one turn automatically, or returns an explicit non-actionable delivery state/blocker; successful send output cannot leave prompt text indefinitely awaiting external Enter input.
notes: The underlying screen-parser failure is broader than a missing Enter: Antigravity was at a ready empty prompt, but hcom reported tui:prompt-has-text because it treated the visible accept-edits mode banner as input_text. Delivery therefore remained queued and even a standalone Enter did not submit the intended message. Regression coverage must include this exact banner.
close_reason: Fixed the Antigravity screen-parser false positive: the agy mode banners (accept-edits/plan/best-of-N) rendered on the empty prompt row are now recognized as placeholder text (exact-match plus wrapped-prefix match), so a ready idle prompt parses as empty instead of tui:prompt-has-text. Delivery then follows the existing inject->Enter->verify state machine and schedules exactly one turn automatically; the parser fix also restores phase-2 clear detection and submit-edge stamping after Enter. Added regression tests for the exact accept-edits banner (non-dim render, with/without ready footer), plan/best-of-N banners, wrapped narrow-pane prefix, head-only typed text staying input, banner-after-submit emptiness, update_delivery_state wiring incl. submit-edge stamping, and the gate passing on the banner-derived empty prompt. Focused tests, fmt --check, cargo check --workspace --all-targets, and clippy -D warnings all pass; the 6 hooks::claude full-suite failures reproduce identically at clean HEAD (pre-existing environmental).

title: Add provider-neutral isolated worker workspaces
description: Delegated hcom workers are blocked by provider workspace-trust, routine approval prompts, and unreliable provider-native sandboxes. Add a fail-closed hcom-owned isolation boundary for PTY-backed interactive and optional high-level workflows, with host-owned scoped messaging and progress, beginning with Antigravity and Claude-backed GLM on Linux/NixOS.
design: Use provider-neutral IsolationProfile and serializable plans with explicit workload trust, stable workflow-policy identity, and attempt-specific identity. Enforce Bubblewrap at the PTY provider-child spawn seam, retain supervision and SQLite on the host, expose a narrow per-run broker for normal hcom messages/events/results, keep Git read-only by default, require dedicated disposable Git state for workspace-git, and never fall back to host execution. Keep workflow identity independent from workspace ownership so explicit sharing can be designed later.
acceptance_criteria: OpenSpec artifacts define observable requirements and phased tasks; hcom diagnoses and explains trust and isolation plans; Bubblewrap preflight rejects unsafe versions; fake-provider tests prove filesystem/process/PTY containment; sandboxed workers cannot access hcom databases but remain reachable through ordinary messaging and compact streams; normal interactive Antigravity and Claude/GLM runs complete without routine prompts; scoped GitHub operations are enforced by credentials or brokers; resume preserves policy identity while rotating attempt identity; untrusted workloads remain disabled pending egress and credential hardening.
notes: Planning source: openspec/changes/add-isolated-worker-workspaces/. Host Bubblewrap 0.11.2 remains below the required >=0.12.0 security gate. The plan was amended on 2026-09-15 after live workflow testing: hcom run is optional, normal interactive messaging and compact progress must survive isolation, SQLite remains host-owned behind a scoped broker, workload trust is explicit, resume separates policy and attempt identities, and workspace-git requires dedicated disposable Git state. Future opt-in workspace sharing must remain architecturally possible, but coordination details are intentionally undecided. Earlier P0 orchestration prerequisites hcom-f6g.9 through hcom-f6g.11 remain historical context.

# Local feature inventory against latest upstream

Inventory checkpoint: upstream `f687a9cf71d3fdfc5bde2634f2ffcd19520d6a14`, local `e215adc1c0045077cb7abcbe5ae40c20dee2b0d7`, common base `79ebde134c4d29b5ba64e5c9839a12bedb7ee125`. Upstream has 148 commits absent from local HEAD. The prior 77-commit selective inventory remains separately pinned and intact.

A clean upstream base is a plausible way to reduce repeated integration work. The maintained delta should be defined by behavior, with focused ports at current upstream seams. This inventory does not prove that the port will be small or conflict-free: Hermes and orchestration touch shared runtime paths, and native participation needs ownership and hook compatibility work.

| Area | Disposition on a fresh upstream base |
|---|---|
| Hermes provider | Carry the surviving backend extension, hook bridge, lifecycle, launch/resume and transcript behavior; adapt to current upstream APIs. |
| Orchestration | Carry distinct filtered waits, result/progress reporting, thread membership and approval ownership contracts identified below. Preserve newer upstream fixes too. |
| Native participation | Preserve local Claude/Codex participation capabilities with explicit authoritative ownership; gaps are not permission to drop them. |
| Claude lineage/generations | Use current upstream implementation; do not copy the redundant local machinery. |
| Small correctness patches | Carry transcript PATH diagnostics and the recent binding transaction/canonical-owner fixes only where current upstream lacks them. |
| Profiles and workflows | Keep user scripts, model router, permission preference and repository guidance as separate assets where supported. |
| Isolation | Out of rebuild scope by user instruction; keep original design/types as reference only. |
| Retired experiments | Do not revive passive transcript-marker binding or reverted Hermes mesh/dashboard experiments. Archive the inactive GitHub prototype. |

## Maintenance approach

Start from the pinned upstream source and preserve its improvements. Port shared correctness and orchestration contracts at their current interfaces; adapt native participation to current per-run hook installation and ownership rules; then integrate Hermes through explicit provider seams. Keep independent profiles/scripts and inactive design assets separate. Each port needs focused regression checks plus integration gates and review. Candidate small fixes can be offered upstream later, but this inventory does not publish or submit anything.

The list below contains implementation seams as well as feature domains; its entry count is not a count of independent product features. `partial` means upstream supplies only some required behavior. `config-only` means a separate asset/profile rather than a core source port. `upstream-baseline` records provenance, not an assertion that all old accepted adaptations are identical to current upstream.

## Verification and limits

Tier 2 graph-assisted source verification used the original checkout index and direct source reads for the unindexed latest upstream snapshot and dirty integration checkout. All 70 original runtime/test delta paths had no recorded graph gaps; absence of gaps is not proof of completeness. No provider sessions, Windows runtime, sandbox runtime or newly ported test suite were exercised. Existing tests are acceptance contracts to reuse, not test results for a port that has not happened. Both source checkouts were preserved; no staging, commit, push or remote Dolt sync was performed. Durable tracking and the complete structured inventory are saved under Beads `hcom-x5v.15`.

title: Provision Hermes backend integration through hcom hooks setup
description: Current hcom hooks add/status/launch deliberately exclude Hermes and require an externally installed Python plugin. Replace that prerequisite with hcom-owned backend setup for shared Hermes CLI/TUI/serve, with per-session identity and delivery; do not include Desktop UI plugin code. The installed Hermes runtime supports shell hooks for lifecycle/pre_llm_call, while starting a turn in an idle live session requires an additional session-scoped input path. Decide the smallest supported backend mechanism with user before implementation. Preserve existing config and explicit Hermes hook consent.
design: Implement a hcom-owned Hermes backend extension, not Desktop UI. Keep bridge state and notify endpoints per Hermes session ID, not process-global. Use a session-scoped, read-only/explicit-participation binding path so normal Hermes sessions do not auto-mint hcom rows; hcom-launched interactive sessions may bind their launch placeholder. Deliver hcom mail through Hermes PluginContext.inject_message with the durable session key (same as agent.session_id for TUI/serve), so the message is a visible user turn; only acknowledge after host accepts. Require allow_gateway_injection permission for TUI/serve and verify it during readiness. Treat on_session_reset as a boundary that may occur on resume, not unconditional stop; test interleaved serve sessions and reset/resume. Installer must refuse to overwrite the existing externally managed ~/.hermes/plugins/hcom files; test in isolated HERMES_HOME before any live migration. Preserve other CLI behavior.

title: Return a typed Antigravity workspace-trust blocker
description:

Generic launch-blocker classification now recognizes distinctive trust wording, but the Antigravity path and exact live screen have not been proven end to end. This fix must only surface the provider decision; it must not approve trust, inject confirmation keys, or mutate provider trust state.

## Steps to Reproduce
Launch Antigravity through hcom in a fresh workspace that Antigravity has not trusted. Leave the trust decision unanswered. Observe whether hcom promptly publishes a workspace_trust launch blocker with the prompt evidence or continues reporting an apparently live/launching worker.

notes:
Deterministic coverage landed 2026-09-08 (no production code change needed): src/pty/screen.rs renders a realistic Antigravity workspace-trust dialog fixture (VS Code-family wording, one of the distinctive prompts) and locks its exact visible_tail(10,1000) via ANTIGRAVITY_TRUST_DIALOG_TAIL; src/pty/shared.rs proves update_delivery_state publishes that tail during the launch phase with approval=false (trust gate is not a permission approval); src/delivery.rs drives drive_launch_outcome with an unsettled screen and verifies the first-tick typed blocker: instance -> blocked/launch_blocked, wait_for_launch returns Blocked with correlated blocked_records kind=workspace_trust, evidence='Do you trust the authors of the files in this workspace?', reason=screen_settled_not_ready, ready=0. Negative test: ordinary task text mentioning workspace trust stays Pending while unsettled and classifies unknown when settled, never workspace_trust. Checks: 5 new tests pass, cargo fmt --check clean, cargo check --workspace --all-targets clean, clippy -D warnings clean. Pre-existing unrelated failures: 6 hooks::claude tests fail identically at HEAD; tools::codex_preprocessing flakes rotate run-to-run (verified in temp worktree at HEAD). Remaining: fresh untrusted-workspace live run to confirm the real agy trust screen wording/wrapping reaches the classifier on a single line (line-based matcher may miss wrapped question rows).
Live verification completed 2026-09-08. First fresh-workspace run (batch 38e4edf2) reproduced current Antigravity wording, 'Do you trust the contents of this project?', but classified it as unknown, proving the original fixture was stale. Added that exact distinctive prompt and updated the rendered fixture. After cargo fmt, targeted regression tests, cargo check --workspace --all-targets, and clippy -D warnings passed, a second fresh untrusted workspace run (batch e314648c) terminated the high-level wait with blocked status and returned a correlated record: kind=workspace_trust, evidence='Do you trust the contents of this project?', reason=screen_settled_not_ready. No trust approval, input injection, or provider trust-state mutation occurred. Independent review found no code defects.

title: Align Hermes HERMES_HOME transcript resolver with runtime directory semantics
description: Installed Hermes hermes_constants.py get_process_hermes_home trims HERMES_HOME, and hermes_state.py computes get_hermes_home() / state.db. title: Ordinary Hermes command attribution: native detection + session-binding identity
description: Installed Hermes exports HERMES_SESSION_ID into each terminal subprocess (tools/environments/local.py _inject_session_context_env), but hcom cannot attribute an ordinary command inside a bound Hermes session: src/shared/tool_detection.rs has no Hermes rule (detect_tool falls back to Tool::Adhoc), src/router.rs only reads CODEX_THREAD_ID, and src/identity.rs has only wrapperless Codex lookup — so hcom send/list resolve no self identity there. Implement in owned files only (tool_detection.rs, router.rs, cli_context.rs, identity.rs + focused tests): a Hermes native detection rule on HERMES_SESSION_ID with clean_for_child marker, and a session-binding lookup that ONLY accepts existing hermes-owned rows, preserves explicit name/process precedence and all other tool behavior, never adopts or binds on an arbitrary command, and fails safely (no identity) for stale/unknown session ids. No edits to hooks/hermes.rs, launcher.rs, integration_spec.rs, or the plugin. Focused tests + fmt + clippy; no commit/push.
close_reason: Ordinary Hermes command attribution implemented in the four owned files. tool_detection: HERMES_SESSION_ID native rule (NonEmpty, last among natives so nested tools win) + HCOM_TOOL=hermes fallback, HERMES_SESSION_ID added to child scrub set via tool_marker_vars. identity: pure resolve_hermes_session_identity — only an existing session binding to a live hermes-owned row resolves; stale/unknown/foreign fail safe to None; never binds/adopts. cli_context+router: HERMES_SESSION_ID read in router and threaded through build_ctx_for_command as last-resort fallback, gated on env-detected Tool::Hermes (nested foreign tools with leaked marker refuse), excluded for start (it deletes the identity it resolves) and whenever HCOM_PROCESS_ID is present. Verified: 98 focused tests, 1129 serial tests across shared/commands/cli_context/identity/router/hooks, fmt+clippy clean, end-to-end binary smoke test (attributed send from tapa, list 'Your name: tapa', stale/nested/no-env all fail safe). Not committed.

title: Harden hermes hook adapter: --name gating, ack cursor truthfulness, ack-0 noop
description: Audit of src/hooks/hermes.rs found the argv RPC write paths accept any --name. Demonstrable defects: (1) hermes-status/hermes-stop/hermes-beforetool on an unknown name still emit status events into the shared stream for a nonexistent instance (set_status logs even when its UPDATE touches no row); (2) the same RPCs on a name owned by another tool overwrite/finalize (delete) that tool's instance row — cross-tool interference from the Hermes plugin; (3) hermes-read --ack --up-to on an unknown instance returns {"acked_to": N} while update_instance_fields is UPDATE-only, so no row is written — a false success; (4) --format replies up_to:0 on an empty inbox but --ack --up-to 0 is an error, so a plugin that acks the format cursor fails on every empty read; (5) --session-id "" is treated as present and falls through to a misleading bind error; (6) unparseable --notify-port is silently dropped. Fix scope is src/hooks/hermes.rs only: gate write paths on an existing hermes-owned row, make ack 0 a monotonic no-op, reject empty session id, log invalid notify port. Focused serial tests for ordinary binding, cursor safety, lifecycle reset, and status.
close_reason: Hermes-local hardening of src/hooks/hermes.rs complete: write RPCs gated on existing hermes-owned rows (no ghost status events, no cross-tool writes, no false ack success), ack --up-to 0 is a monotonic no-op, empty --session-id rejected, invalid --notify-port logged. 7 new focused tests; hooks::hermes 19/19 and serial hooks:: 436 passed / 0 failed. Not committed per instructions.

title: Make missing-search-tool handling robust to inaccessible PATH entries
description: The test commands::transcript::tests::missing_search_tool_is_an_error_not_an_empty_result fails deterministically on the current WSL host. strace shows every candidate executable is absent, but one PATH directory (/mnt/c/ProgramData/chocolatey/bin) returns EACCES, so std::process::Command reports PermissionDenied instead of NotFound and run_search_tool emits could not run rather than the intended missing-tool diagnostic. This is unrelated to OpenSpec task 3.3 but prevents a clean full binary test run on hosts with inaccessible PATH entries.
acceptance_criteria: Missing external search programs produce the actionable required search tool was not found on PATH diagnostic even when one or more PATH entries are inaccessible, without hiding a permission error for a real executable; the focused transcript test and full binary suite pass on the affected host.
notes:
Review/simplify pass on uncommitted implementation in src/commands/transcript.rs (2026-09-15): helper reduced from 4 fns (~85 lines) to 2 (~38) by reusing terminal::which_candidates for PATHEXT enumeration and dropping the duplicated explicit-path branch (run_search_tool's is_bare_name check is authoritative); is_candidate_file collapsed to one metadata call + Path::is_symlink, preserving EACCES-symlink-target semantics. Bare-name PermissionDenied with no candidate on PATH -> 'was not found on PATH'; real candidate (incl. non-executable) or explicit path -> 'could not run'. Tests: deterministic helper scan, serial EnvGuard E2E (WSL PATH shape), new explicit-path E2E. Gates: transcript 29/29, fmt clean, check --locked --workspace --all-targets clean, clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings clean, full binary suite green 2440/0. Intermittent unrelated parallel-test failures observed in isolation-work tests (omp install, codex local_scan, start rebind) — pass in isolation, scatter randomly; pre-existing, worth a separate bead.
2026-09-15 implementation complete after Gemini then GLM handoff. Gemini confirmed glibc execvp/EACCES behavior and implemented the core fix; GLM reused terminal::which_candidates, reduced the patch from 245 to 197 added lines, removed redundant path/PATHEXT logic, and added explicit-path coverage. Parent verification: 29 transcript tests pass; isolated launcher flake passes; fmt, locked workspace check, strict Clippy, and diff check pass. Independent review approved with no blocking findings. GLM had one fully green 2440-test binary run; parent run passed 2439 with one unrelated launcher shared-state flake that passed immediately in isolation.

title: Wake only resolved recipients after targeted sends
description:
Tracker item 29: the send path resolves an exact delivered_to set but still calls the system-wide wake_all helper, waking unrelated delivery loops for targeted and thread-resolved messages. This creates avoidable activity and notification work even though only declared recipients can consume the message.

## Steps to Reproduce
Register wake endpoints for at least two local agents, send a message targeted only to one agent, and observe that the send path calls wake_all and connects to both wake endpoints even though delivered_to contains only the intended recipient.
acceptance_criteria: Targeted and thread-resolved sends wake only their resolved local recipients and any explicitly required coordinator; explicit broadcasts retain fan-out; remote relay behavior remains correct; unavailable/stopped recipients remain safe; deterministic endpoint tests prove unrelated agents receive no wake while intended recipients still deliver promptly.
close_reason: Targeted and thread-resolved sends now wake only resolved local recipients; explicit broadcasts retain fan-out and relay behavior. Deterministic endpoint tests, send/wake suites, workspace check, strict Clippy, and review pass.

title: Distinguish transient Hermes read failures from stale session attribution
description: Hermes hook session_attribution_matches maps get_instance_full read errors to a false match. hermes-read --format or --ack can then return the same no-longer-attributed error as a verified rebind, causing the backend extension to tear down a valid listener on a transient DB error. It self-heals on later discovery but can delay mail. Keep fail-closed behavior while distinguishing read failure from verified stale attribution.
acceptance_criteria: Read error produces a distinguishable retryable response; verified rebind still tears down stale state; transient read failure retains the active listener and retries with backoff; focused Rust and Python tests pass.

title: Harden legacy Hermes hook start lock window

Existing-only enrollment now holds the lock through those writes, but restructuring the older path was deferred to avoid changing established behavior in the backend-extension patch.
acceptance_criteria: Legacy no-process start and competing Hermes enrollment cannot interleave between identity resolution and attribution/notify writes; preserve legacy start semantics and cover lock lifetime with focused tests.
